ConfidenceBreakdownSchema.description:
The propagated-confidence composition (system input #6). Mirrors
``app.ml.inference.ConfidenceBreakdown`` field-for-field: three served signals (distance from
the NULL ceiling, distance from the AMBIGUOUS entropy boundary, calibrated max-probability) and
their product. Presentational — the gate's ``confidence_state`` stays authoritative.
ConfidenceBreakdownSchema.title: ConfidenceBreakdownSchema

ConfidenceState.description:
Explicit confidence / uncertainty state for a classifier prediction.

Mirrors the ``predictions.confidence_state`` column (master spec §8.4) and adds
``OUT_OF_DISTRIBUTION`` — the style-space state (§5.2) that the project
constitution lists as a mandatory uncertainty state (non-negotiable #4). The
classifier never returns a forced label below the confidence gate; it returns
one of these states instead.
ConfidenceState.title: ConfidenceState

DriverProfileSchema.description:
Dataset + evaluation facts for one driver, sourced from ``driver_profiles.json``.

Every optional field is ``None`` for an honest "not measured", never 0.0: a driver with too few
laps for a within-session SD and a driver who laps identically every time must not render the
same. ``identification_f1`` is the champion's **held-out** per-driver F1 — a driver the summary
never scored keeps ``None`` rather than borrowing a training-split number.
DriverProfileSchema.title: DriverProfileSchema

DriverSignalSchema.description:
One feature the champion attributes most to a driver, plus where they rank on it.

``attribution`` is mean |SHAP| — a magnitude, so it never implies a direction. ``percentile`` is
the driver's rank on that feature against the rest of the grid (0 = lowest mean, 1 = highest)
and is ``None`` when the profiles artefact carries no rank, so the screen names the feature
without claiming which way it points.
DriverSignalSchema.title: DriverSignalSchema

ErrorCode.description: Every named error code, flag, fallback, and warning in the APEX spec.
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

IngestSessionRequest.description: POST /ingest/session body — the FastF1 session coordinates to ingest async (§8.5).
IngestSessionRequest.title: IngestSessionRequest

ReplayAlert.description:
The F10 ``DegradationAlert`` as of one replayed lap (§5.3 / §10.7 banner payload). Mirrors
``app.monitoring.detector.DegradationAlert`` field-for-field; closes the F19 alert seam
(div #74) — the route used to drop it.
ReplayAlert.title: ReplayAlert

SampleSegmentSchema.description:
One real held-out lap for the Prediction screen's picker (profiles artefact). The raw
per-lap features go straight back into POST /predict; ``true_driver`` is the matrix's ground
truth so the screen can grade the prediction — a held-out lap, so grading it is a genuine
generalisation test, not a replay of training data.
SampleSegmentSchema.title: SampleSegmentSchema

SessionDriverSchema.description: One driver's presence in a persisted session (code + how many laps are replayable).
SessionDriverSchema.title: SessionDriverSchema

SessionSummary.description:
One catalog row for ``GET /sessions`` — the Screen 6 session picker (closes F19 div #77:
sessions were listed nowhere, forcing a raw UUID input).
SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary

TyreCompoundStatsSchema.description:
Stint-degradation statistics for one (driver, compound), from clean train laps.

All pace numbers are **net** within-stint drift: the matrix carries no fuel-load channel, so
fuel burn (which makes cars faster) and tyre wear (slower) are combined, and the true tyre
component is larger than each number — the screen states this rather than correcting it with
an invented constant. ``cliff_age`` is ``None`` when no acceleration past the linear trend was
detected; most curves are near-linear and a decorative cliff would be detection theatre.
``f27_median``/``f28_median`` are the pipeline's own behavioural tyre-age slopes (throttle /
brake adaptation per lap of age).
TyreCompoundStatsSchema.title: TyreCompoundStatsSchema

TyreCurvePointSchema.description:
One tyre age on the aggregated degradation curve: the median lap-time delta versus each
stint's own early-lap baseline, with the IQR and the lap count behind the point.
TyreCurvePointSchema.title: TyreCurvePointSchema

TyreWearResponse.description:
GET /tyres — per-driver, per-compound stint degradation from the profiles artefact.
``drivers`` is empty when the artefact is absent (the screen explains, nothing is invented).
TyreWearResponse.title: TyreWearResponse

get.description:
200 always — an empty array if the fingerprints table is empty (§8.5). Deterministic: each
driver's radar is its LATEST (season, circuit) row, matching /fingerprint and /compare (§11).

The DB supplies identity + radar; the startup-loaded profiles artefact supplies the lap counts,
lap-time consistency and per-driver held-out F1. The two are independent — an absent artefact
leaves ``profile`` null and ``signature`` empty without touching the rest of the row, so this
endpoint never fails because a *supplementary* source is missing.

Report DB + model-handle status. Critical = DB connected AND every model ready; cache
(Redis, F14) is reported but never critical. Any critical failure → HTTP 503.

post.description:
Enqueue an async session ingestion → 202 Accepted (§8.5). Counts are *pending* placeholders;
poll ``/ingest/status/{session_id}`` for progress and the terminal quality report.

get.description:
Report a job's status (§8.5). 404 if unknown. On COMPLETE, ``result`` carries the terminal
report (the §8.5 counts + quality_report) so the async response fulfils the master contract.

Replay a persisted stint through the degradation detector (§10.7). 200 full · 206 partial ·
404 unknown.

The curated held-out sample laps for the Prediction screen. 200 with [] when the profiles
artefact is absent — the screen then explains there is nothing to pick, exactly like an empty
driver grid; a missing *demo* source is not a service failure.
List persisted sessions with their replayable drivers (newest season/round first).

Per-driver, per-compound stint degradation (Screen 4). Served from the startup-loaded
profiles artefact; absent artefact → an empty map, never fabricated curves. A malformed
per-compound block is skipped WITH a data_quality_log row — a screen fed by this endpoint
can trust every curve it does receive.
